mutants.why: The other end of gate two. CONTROL-1 and CONTROL-2 prove the harness reports BROKEN when it cannot get a result; this proves it reports SURVIVED from a run that really happened, rather than only ever being able to say BROKEN or KILLED.

mutants.name: 2730-e: Start's general guard narrowed to Running only
2730-o: a roster that carries no session list is accepted again (positive zero)
2730-p: an EXPLICIT empty session list is refused too (the over-correction)
2730-q: the update owner's hold is disabled (the mutation that reached a commit)
mutants.why: Expected BROKEN, and the reason is worth more than a kill would be. With the hold removed the update owner proceeds PAST it and attempts a real install, which CRASHES THE TEST HOST - 'Test host process crashed', 9 tests reported and the run aborted. A crash is not a test failure, so the harness correctly refuses a verdict rather than recording KILLED or SURVIVED. The crash is itself the evidence that the hold guards something drastic: everything beyond it is the install path. It also says the test rig would drive a real update apply if that hold ever regressed, which is recorded as a hazard rather than left as a surprise.
